question: Since the EU-Andean Trade Agreement (EU-Colombia, Ecuador, Peru Trade Agreement) entered into force in 2013, the geopolitical and economic environment has changed fundamentally. The EU now faces increasing supply chain vulnerabilities, intensified competition over critical raw materials and a rapid digital transformation.

In this context, relations with the Andean partners need to evolve from a traditional trade relationship into a mutually beneficial strategic partnership. A modernised and forward-looking framework under the EU-Andean Trade Agreement could reinforce competitiveness, resilience and longterm economic cooperation on a strategic basis. In the light of this: 1.
Does the Commission intend to launch a formal evaluation of the EU-Andean Trade Agreement with a view to transforming it into a modern strategic partnership framework?

Is the Commission considering the inclusion of new chapters covering critical raw materials, digital trade, regulatory cooperation and dedicated small and medium enterprises facilitation mechanisms to strengthen the strategic dimension of the Agreement?

Will the Commission request that the Council swiftly grant a negotiating mandate to modernise the EU-Andean Trade Agreement and align it with the EU’s current strategic, industrial and economic priorities?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.4.2026) The Trade Agreement between the EU and Colombia, Ecuador and Peru1 entered into force on 1 November 2024. The Commission agrees with the Honourable Member that it would now be appropriate to initiate a reflection on how the Agreement fits with the current geopolitical and economic environment.

Regarding the transformation into a modern strategic partnership, the Commission committed in the 2022 Joint Communication ‘A New Agenda for EU-Latin America and Caribbean Relations’2 to discuss the possible upgrade of the Agreement's provisions on sustainable development. To this end, the EU and the Andean countries have established a Working Group under the relevant Committee where discussions are still ongoing.

A broader modernisation of the agreement could be considered. The Commission is exploring with various partners to extend the trade and economic cooperation to new fields. Any formal request for a negotiating mandate to the Council would require further scoping to ensure alignment with the EU’s strategic priorities. The conclusions of any deliberations in this regard will be fully reported to the European Parliament.
